newsitem.title: USA: Lucent introduces gigabit copper LAN cable.
newsitem.headline: Lucent introduces gigabit copper LAN cable.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc said Monday it had introduced a new copper cable that delivers reliable, high-speed performance at up to one gigabit per second, or six times that of current copper cabling.
A gigabit represents roughly a billion bits of data.
Lucent's said its SYSTIMAX gigaspeed cable would be used to boost the bandwidth capacity on computer local area networks (LAN) to handle data-intensive or multimedia communications.

The company said the SYSTIMAX gigaspeed cable offers significantly improved transmission balancing features that translate into fewer data transmission errors caused by interference between wires in the same cable.
Lucent's gigaspeed cable was designed and developed by its research and development arm, Bell Laboratories.

"The speed of personal computers has increased at a staggering rate, doubling approximately every eighteen months since 1991," said David Laughland, vice president of Global Private Systems at Lucent Technologies.
"Lucent Technologies has designed a solution that will support the growing demand for networks that can accommodate faster computer processors and higher-bandwidth applications."
